5.8 NETWORK DESIGN 
 
a) The Project Implementation Agency (PIA) shall be responsible for the survey, planning, design, 
supply, installation, end-to-end integration, and commissioning of newly deployed and 
upgradation of existing network infrastructure including Optical Fibre Cable (OFC) network. The 
PIA shall be responsible for connectivity across all Gram Panchayats (GP) of BharatNet Phase-
I and Phase-II and ensure upgradation of the existing network infrastructure into ring topology 
with IP-MPLS network. This also includes the scope for newly developed GP time to time during 
contract duration based on discovered rate through this bidding process.  
b) Primarily, the PIA shall plan OFC construction through underground laying. However, wherever, 
the same is not possible, the next alternative shall be ADSS OFC laying preferably using existing 
electricity infrastructure (with prior approval from authority) and under the limited scope boundary 
mentioned in this bid document. The same shall be approved by GFGNL based on 
recommendation of IE with appropriate justification and constraints for underground OFC laying. 
In case it is not feasible to lay the OFC (either underground or ADSS), the PIA shall represent 
the same to the IE. The IE after verifying with the field conditions shall submit the same to 
GFGNL. GFGNL will take a final decision for deployment of alternate technology to connect such 
GPs based on the recommendation of IE and/or its valid field unit report. However, post network 
integration, such GPs shall also be the responsibility of the PIA including its integration with 
State- Network Operation Centre (S-NOC). Upon completion of network integration, the PIA shall 
be solely responsible for the designated Gram Panchayats (GPs) and shall ensure their complete 
operational integration with the State Network Operations Centre (S-NOC) Gandhinagar as well 
as in CNOC-Bangalore/Delhi.  
c) The PIA shall deploy new network infrastructure in this RFP fall under the BharatNet network 
scope, for providing connectivity upto Gram Panchayat (GP) 
d) Based on the network infrastructure to be deployed under this project, all permissions shall be 
obtained by the PIA, as required under Applicable Laws, relevant Applicable Permits, license(s), 
authorization(s) and permissions from Department of Telecom / Government of India/ State 
Governments. 
e) The PIA shall build architecture in two major distinct categories for connectivity across 
all Gram-Panchayats of BharatNet Phase-I and Phase-II in ring architecture. 
Category-1: Access Layer (Gram Panchayat to Sub-Block) 
i. Access layer connectivity is between Gram-Panchayat to Sub-Block node.  
ii. Each GP requires at least two OFC path(1CNO) for establishing ring connectivity to protect 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 152 of 618 
 
 
 
Gram-Panchayat router’s traffic. 
iii. The Network shall be made over sub-Block wise with the GPs.  
iv. PIA shall provide below listed equipment at each GP but not limited to, 
a. IP-MPLS Router with Cards and SFPs,  
b. UPS with batteries power backup,  
c. Towards Downlink: Mini OLT, Equipments for alternate technologies (FSO/UBR/Aerial 
OFC-ADSS), Equipments for Revenue Village connectivity (UBR/6F Aerial Drop) 
d. Transmission Racks, Earthing, MCBs, FDMS etc. 
Note: 
For Village Connectivity( Beyond the GP Connectivity): 
a. Equipments for alternate technologies for Village connectivity’s  (UBR/6F aerial drop), 
b. Earthing, MCBs, OFC compass etc. 
c. Any other additional active,passive equipment as per connectivity medium adopted for 
revenue village connectivity by the bidder. 
v. The above details is for the high level clarification on the bidder’s scope, however considering 
any additional equipment that mentioned (passive/active) require for end deliverables will be 
in the scope of the bidder without any additional cost to tenderer. 
vi. Earthing of any site, GP/Block/Revenue villages should be dedicated and not to use existing  
earth point for safety and to avoid any harm to network elements/humans. However, 
equipment working at existing BharatNet network sites like but not limited to, GP /Shelter if in 
suitable conditions may be use by submission of prior undertaking of safety compliances from 
the bidder.  
vii.  GP (Gram Panchayat) nodes shall be connected using a 10G ring architecture, preferably 
dual‑homed, utilizing maximum three 10G GP OFC rings. Each GP ring should be parented 
on the respective sub‑block node. 
Category-2: Aggregation Layer (Sub-Block to Master-Block/Sub- Block),  
• Aggregation layer connectivity is between Sub-Block to Master-Block/Sub-block.  
• Each block requires at least two OFC Path(1CNO) to protect block router’s traffic.

over by the PIA. 
• Transmission Racks, Earthing & ELCBs (wherever required), MCBs, FDMS etc.

sub-block ring comprising of two/three 100G Sub-Block nodes to be parented on master block in 
dual home architecture. Maximum two Sub-block ring node should be parented on the respective 
Master‑block node. 
 
Category-3: Express/Core Layer / Master block to SDC 
• The Routers and RFMS at Master-block(Co-located at Sub-Block), along with configuration,

cards and SFPs for aggregation of sub-block network, for internet breakout at district level 
shall be made over by the PIA. 
• The ILL/P2P link connectivity of master-Block routers to State NOC/SDC shall be arranged 
by the GFGNL. Further,SDC/State NOC to Central NOC DCN link shall be arrange by GFGNL 
BSNL for which PIA shall not be charged.

5.10 ACCEPTANCE TESTING (COMMISSIONING) FOR THE OPTICAL FIBRE NETWORK 
CONNECTIVITY 
Acceptance Testing Criteria for Dual-Homed Network Architecture 
1. General Provisions 
1.1 The Successful Bidder/PIA shall carry out installation, commissioning, testing, and final 
acceptance of the network comprising Gram Panchayat (GP), Sub-block, and Master Block 
levels in a dual-homed architecture. 
1.2 The network architecture shall ensure that: 
• 
Each Gram Panchayat (GP) is Preferably dual homed to two (2) distinct Sub-blocks, and 
• 
Each Sub-block is Preferably dual homed to two (2) distinct Master Blocks, 
providing redundancy and high availability. 
1.3 The connectivity from Master Block to State Data Centre (SDC)/State NOC/BBNL NOC shall be 
provisioned through third-party ILL/P2P, and the same shall form an integral part of the 
acceptance testing. 
1.4 Final acceptance shall be granted only after successful completion of all tests, including 
redundancy validation, and approval by the State/SIA or its nominated agency. 
 
2. Acceptance Criteria – Master Block 
2.1 Scope of Acceptance 
2.1.1 The acceptance at Master Block level shall cover 100% commissioning of infrastructure, 
connectivity, and services, including: 
• 
Preferably Dual connectivity from Sub-blocks 
• 
Upstream LL connectivity to SDC/NOCs 
• 
End-to-end traffic handling capability 
2.2 Installation and Commissioning 
2.2.1 The PIA shall ensure installation and commissioning of: 
• 
Active network equipment (routers/switches) 
• 
Power supply systems and earthing infrastructure 
• 
Structured cabling and optical fibre termination 
• 
Leased Line termination equipment 
2.2.2 All equipment and infrastructure shall comply with applicable standards and specifications 
defined in the RFP. 
2.3 Connectivity and Traffic Testing 
2.3.1 The PIA shall demonstrate successful traffic flow from: 
• 
Sub-block 1 to Master Block to SDC/NOC 
• 
Sub-block 2 to Master Block to SDC/NOC 
2.3.2 The PIA shall also demonstrate end-to-end connectivity from GP locations through Sub-blocks 
to Master Block and further to SDC/NOCs. 
2.3.3 Traffic shall be tested for: 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 156 of 618 
 
 
 
• 
Throughput 
• 
Latency 
• 
Packet loss 
2.4 Leased Line (LL) Validation 
2.4.1 The PIA shall ensure that the LL connectivity meets the Service Level Agreements (SLAs) 
specified by the service provider. 
2.4.2 The LL shall be tested for: 
• 
Minimum committed bandwidth 
• 
Latency and jitter 
• 
Packet loss 
2.4.3 In case of multiple LL links, the PIA shall demonstrate automatic failover between ILLs/P2P. 
 
2.5 Redundancy and Failover Testing 
2.5.1 The PIA shall conduct failover testing including: 
• 
Failure of one Sub-block link 
• 
Failure of LL link 
2.5.2 The network shall automatically reroute traffic through alternate paths without manual 
intervention. 
2.5.3 There shall be no significant service degradation during failover. 
 
2.6 Optical Fibre Testing 
2.6.1 The PIA shall carry out 100% testing of fibre links from Sub-blocks to Master Block using: 
• 
Optical Time Domain Reflectometer (OTDR) 
• 
Light Source and Power Meter (LSPM) 
2.6.2 Testing shall be conducted at 1310 nm and 1550 nm wavelengths, in both directions. 
2.6.3 Acceptance criteria for attenuation shall be following for the 100% OFC cores connected with 
devices for Master-Block to Sub-Block: 
• 
1310 nm: 0.34 dB/km + 0.1 dB per splice + 1 dB connector loss 
• 
1550 nm: 0.22 dB/km + 0.1 dB per splice + 1 dB connector loss 
2.6.4 Measured attenuation shall be less than the calculated acceptable attenuation. 
 
 
2.7 Final Acceptance Criteria – Master Block 
Acceptance shall be granted only upon: 
• 
Successful operation of dual upstream links 
• 
Compliance of LL connectivity with SLA 
• 
Successful demonstration of failover scenarios 
• 
Submission of all testing reports and documentation 
 
3. Acceptance Criteria – Sub-Block

XVII. When constructing a foundation for a new shelter(if in case), it's crucial to consider several 
following factors to ensure safety and stability but not limited to, 
 
a. Load Bearing Capacity of Soil: This refers to the soil's ability to support the weight of the 
structure without experiencing failure. Different types of soil have varying load-bearing capacities, 
and it's essential to assess this to determine whether a shallow or deep foundation is needed. 
b. Seismic Load: This involves the forces exerted on a structure during an earthquake. Seismic 
load calculations take into account factors such as ground motion, soil type, and the building's 
weight and dynamic characteristics. 
c. Wind Load: Wind load refers to the pressure exerted by wind on a structure. It includes uplift, 
shear, and lateral forces, which must be considered to prevent structural failure, especially in 
areas prone to high winds. 
 
XVIII. Similarly, For rooftop installations at shelter/building, following additional considerations 
needs to include but not limited to, 
Shelter Load Bearing Capacity: The existing structure's ability to support additional weight from 
the new installation must be evaluated. This includes the weight of the new shelter, equipment, and 
any live loads such as people or rain or etc. 
Structural Stability: Ensuring that the shelter can maintain its integrity under the added loads and 
environmental conditions is critical. This involves checking for adequate support, and overall design 
to withstand both static and dynamic forces.

site before start of work from Government approved agency.

recommendation to GFGNL. Based on IE’s recommendation, GFGNL may approve the use 
of alternate technology, ensuring compliance with performance and SLA requirements. 
Implementation shall be at no additional cost to GFGNL. 
I. 
Where neither Underground Fiber nor ADSS cable laying is feasible due to technical or site 
constraints, keeping overall limitation mentioned in this RFP document for alternate

1. 
Tower Construction Requirements 
a) The PIA shall construct self-supporting galvanized steel towers designed in accordance with 
IS 875 (Part 3): Wind Loads, and TIA-222 (Revision H or latest) standards for 
telecommunication tower design. 
b) Towers including the product(clamping) shall be engineered to sustain peak wind velocities of 
up to 180 km/h, including dynamic wind loads, gust factors, and terrain effects. 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 176 of 618 
 
 
 
c) Pole & mast for UBR installation should withstand wind speed of minimum 150 Kmph in normal 
area and minimum 180 Kmph in coastal and Kutch area. Successful bidder has to ensure 
tower earthing, lightening arrestor, aviation lamps and other related components as per 
compliance requirement of DoT. 
d) Structural safety margins must account for antenna loads, feeder cables, maintenance 
platforms, and future load expansions. 
e) Proper grounding, lightning protection systems, and corrosion-resistant coatings must be 
incorporated to ensure long-term operational reliability and compliance with IEC 62305 
standards. 
f) Foundation design shall consider soil investigation reports, seismic zone classification, and 
uplift resistance parameters. 
g) The mast to be used for UBR shall be made of HT Mild Steel angles of E350 grade and or MS 
angles of E250(A) grade confirming to IS:2062/Equivalent ASTM. All steel used shall be hot-
dip galvanized conforming to IS:4759. The mast shall be designed for operational wind speed 
of 180Kmph. Design standard shall be as per is 800-2007. The mast to be installed with 
appropriate plinth and 3/6/9/12/15 Mtr height above ground level to ensure sustained LOS.

2. Optical Wireless Communication (OWC) – LiFi/FSO Systems 
• 
Towers for LiFi/Free Space Optics (FSO) shall be constructed to ensure precise optical 
beam alignment, minimizing divergence and dispersion across communication endpoints. 
• 
A four-legged lattice tower including the product(clamping) design is mandatory to provide 
enhanced torsional rigidity, reduce oscillations, and eliminate micro-vibrations that affect 
optical signal coherence. 
• 
The design must meet EN 1993 (Eurocode 3) structural standards or equivalent Indian 
design codes, with additional damping mechanisms if required to maintain optomechanical 
stability. 
• 
Towers must be equipped with anti-reflective platforms, vibration dampers, and mounting 
provisions for active beam alignment systems where applicable. 
• 
Environmental durability must be validated for high-altitude, coastal, or humid regions, with 
towers certified to withstand temperature variations, UV exposure, and 180 km/h wind 
speeds as per ASTM E330 or equivalent. 
• 
Provisions for power backup systems (UPS, solar integration) and secure equipment 
enclosures for OWC transceivers shall also be included.

5.15 SCOPE OF WORK FOR  STATE- NETWORK OPERATIONS CENTRE (S-NOC) 
IMPLEMENTATION 
           
1. GFGNL has already established S-NOC with state of art facilities at Udyogbhavan, Gandhinagar 
as part of the BharatNet Phase-II. The PIA will be required to upgrade these S-NOCs in 
accordance with the functional requirements mentioned below, by suitably modifying the 
indicative BoM (RFP Clause_9.44) after obtaining the approval from GFGNL/IE.The Active, IT 
and Non IT component list given in (clause 9.36) Annexure-XXXVI. This infrastructure can be 
utilized/upgrade/replaced to meet the requirements of ABP.GFGNL shall provide the space and 
power at SDC/SNOC.Note: The existing IT and Non-IT infrastructure listed in Annexure-XXXVI 
is not included as a separate payable item under the Financial Bid. The Bidder shall, at its own 
cost and without any additional financial implication to GFGNL, upgrade, augment, modify, 
repair, replace, or supplement the existing infrastructure, wherever required, to meet the 
functional, technical, capacity, availability, security, and SLA requirements of the Amended 
BharatNet Program. No claim for any additional payment under this account shall be considered 
of extra line items by GFGNL during the entire contract period. 
2. BharatNet State Network Operation Centre (S-NOC) shall be required to monitor the up time, 
qualitative parameters of the BharatNet network and provisioning of the services as mentioned 
in the RFP. The fundamental purpose of this RFP is to provide technology led governance of the 
entire network including automation in service provisioning, scanning of the network health, 
digital routes for identifying fiber location, digital measurement book, digital SLA and top 
management level dashboard. The IT infrastructure at S-NOC shall be in full redundancy 
architecture and will be provisioned with the required storage, computing, networking, security, 
backup, monitoring, management and help desk components. 
3. PIA shall be responsible for establishing of an S-NOC for managing the existing (Phase-I & II, 
to be upgraded) and new network (to be created) in Gujarat State. The PIA shall be responsible 
for the deployment of all requisite hardware, software, and manpower for monitoring, helpdesk, 
troubleshooting, etc.  
4. The scope shall also include design, supply, installation, testing, commissioning, documentation, 
operations and maintenance of NOC along with workforce deployment, training, etc.  
5. The NOC shall be capable to perform key functions but not limited to i.e. fault management, 
performance management, configuration management and security management etc.  
6. PIA shall submit details such as APIs', protocols, version, attributes etc. to GFGNL. Once, the 
information has been shared at detailed level, both PIA and GFGNL shall complete integration 
of NOC within 90 days from agreement signed date.

Amended BharatNet Program. The S-NOC solution shall comprise a tightly integrated suite of 
Network Management System (NMS), Operations Support System (OSS), Business 
Support System (BSS), Customer Relationship Management (CRM), and Helpdesk &

IV. 
The solution shall provide centralized, real-time visibility of BharatNet infrastructure and services

detection, trouble ticketing, SLA monitoring, MTTR tracking and escalation; support utilization,

related to BharatNet services and infrastructure. 
V. 
The integrated S-NOC platform shall support role-based access, secure data exchange, open 
standards-based integration with network equipment, GIS systems and the Central NOC 
(C-NOC), and shall generate operational, SLA, utilization and grievance reports as required by

4 Warranty Support:  
As part of the warranty services PIA shall provide: 
1.  PIA shall provide a comprehensive on-site OEM warranty of 10 years. warranty from 
(SI/OEM) as per the MAF. 
2. Extended warranty can be provided by PIA on his own risk and cost basis. 
3. PIA shall provide the comprehensive manufacturer’s warranty and support in respect of 
proper design, quality and workmanship of all hardware, equipment, accessories etc. covered 
by the bid. PIA must warrant all hardware, equipment, accessories, spare parts, software etc. 
procured and implemented as per this bid against any manufacturing defects during the 
warranty period. 
4. PIA shall provide the performance warranty in respect of performance of the installed 
hardware and software to meet the performance requirements and service levels in the bid. 
5. PIA is responsible for sizing and procuring the necessary hardware and software licenses as 
per the performance requirements provided in the bid. 
6. During the warranty period PIA shall replace or augment or procure higher level new 
equipment or additional licenses at no additional cost in case the procured hardware or 
software is not adequate to meet the service levels. 
7. If the solution fully /partially fails during FAT, the PIA must repair or replace by equivalent or 
higher-level of new equipment at no cost to the tenderer after approval from GFGNL/GSDC. 
8. Mean Time between Failures (MTBF): If during contract period, any equipment has a 
hardware failure on four or more occasions in a period of less than three months, it shall be 
replaced by equivalent or higher-level of new equipment by the PIA at no cost.For any delay 
in arrangement of replacement / repaired equipment’s for inspection, delivery of equipment’s 
or for commissioning of the systems or for acceptance tests / checks at each/ any site; GFGNL 
reserves the right tocharge a penalty. 
9. During the warranty period, the PIA shall maintain the systems and repair / replace the 
components to keep the solution operational at the installed site at no extra charges to the 
organization. 
10. The PIA shall as far as possible repair/ replace the equipment at site. 
11. Warranty should not become void, if DST/GILGFGNL buys, any other supplemental hardware 
from a third party and installs it within these machines under intimation to the PIA. However, 
the warranty will not apply to such supplemental hardware items installed. 
12. PIA shall monitor warranties to check adherence to preventive and repair maintenance terms 
and conditions. 
13. PIA shall ensure that the warranty complies with the agreed Technical Standards, Security 
Requirements, Operating Procedures, and Recovery Procedures. 
14. PIA shall have to stock and provide adequate onsite and offsite spare parts and spare 
component to ensure that the uptime commitment as per SLA is met. 
15. Any component that is reported to be down on a given date should be either fully repaired or 
replaced by temporary substitute (of equivalent configuration) within the time frame indicated 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 198 of 618 
 
 
 
in the Service Level Agreement (SLA). 
16. PIA shall develop and maintain an inventory database to include the registered hardware 
warranties. 
17. To provide warranty support effectively, OEM should have spare depo in India and will be 
asked to deliver spare as per SLA requirement. 
18. Management should be in HA, and required hardware, software, license and other 
components should be provided by PIA from the day-01. 
19. Design, implementation should be done by OEM. 
20. MIS reports should be submitted by PIAs as and when asked by GFGNL. 
21. The bidder shall provide a centralized Data Analytics Platform capable of collecting, storing,

5.16 VIDEOGRAPHY  
5.16.1 Videography for all the works like trenching, fibre laying, splicing etc shall be conducted by 
PIA. The Video Recording (with Date/ Time stamping and GPS coordinates) of the OFC laying 
and Ducting works by the PIA shall be done in following phases as under- 
a) Ducting - Video recording of Open Trenches is to be done using a Vertical Measuring Stick 
(Known as Measuring Staff in Civil Engineering Terms) at every 50 (Fifty) Mtr intervals. The 
depth reading in the Staff from top of the duct should be clearly recorded. In case of HDD (if 
the PIA is not using the machine recorded depth and produce the depth data), the depth of 
Entry & Exit pits should be Video recorded from top of the duct. The Couplers, Plugs and 
End Caps wherever required as per E.I. should also be captured in the video. Protection 
used as per E.I. in case of Low Depth should also be Video Recorded. 
b) OFC Blowing/ Pulling - The OFC blowing process should be Photographed (geo tagged with 
time stamp) clearly showing the drum and fibre meter reading details. 
c) Splicing- The splicing should be Photographed (geo tagged with time stamp) clearly showing 
that all 24F/48 F have been spliced and arranged in cassette. 
d) Man Hole/ Cable Chamber- The Cable Chamber of MH base should be Photographed ( geo 
tagged with time stamp) clearly showing the base plate of 50 mm thickness, RCC joint 
Chamber and Top Cover as per E.I. The cable loop also to be video recorded – showing 
start and end readings. 
e) Route Markers- Route Markers should be photographed (geo tagged with time stamp). 
5.16.2 All Videos/ Photographs (geo tagged with time stamp) shall be submitted /uploaded with a 
unique location related name in a folder with file descriptions clearly indicating each of the 
above activities like Ducting, Blowing, Splicing, MH/CC & RM. 
5.16.3 The MP4 Video should have 3 windows running concurrently for following views- 
(a) 
Window 1 – Physical work being carried out with Lat/ Long and Date/Time stamp 
(b) Window 2 – Location of the activity on Google Map. 
(c) 
Window 3 – KMZ/KML file with chainage, OFC route, Depth, Offset from road centre & Lat/ 
Long of Joint pits etc. 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 200 of 618 
 
 
 
5.16.4 Each Video file should be of at least 2 minutes time duration capturing works being done for 
40 Mtrs in case of Open Trenching and one shot in case of HDD. The size of each Video file 
should not be more than 30MB so that the same can be sent through mobile/mail etc. 
5.16.5 The speed of movement of the camera while recording the Video should be maximum 
20Mtr/Minute. 
5.16.6 All Video recordings should be done in day light time without rain, fog, mist etc. Wherever, the 
video recording is not possible, photographs should be taken at every 10 meters with the 
approval of GFGNL/IE. 
5.16.7 The nomenclature of the files should be in the following format:-XXXX_YYYYY: 12345_67890: 
Work 
XXXX is the Route Abbreviation as per the Work Order 
YYYYY is the Circle+District+Block Abbreviation as per the Work Order 12345 is the 
Chainage of start point of Video Recording 
67890 is Chainage of end point of Video Recording 
Work- OT Ducting- OTD, HDD, OFC Blowing- OFB, Splicing- OFC, MM/CC, RM etc. 
5.16.8 Sub-Block end should be Chainage ‘0’ and GP end should be taken as the last Chainage. 
5.16.9 The Backend team of the PIA should merge all the files of a section of 40 meters in 
succession or HDD shot and send to  GFGNL and IE for review / verification of works and 
GIS NOC Delhi for linking the same with GIS. 
5.16.10 The payments of the works as per payment schedule mentioned in the tender shall only be 
done if the videos /photographs (geo tagged with time stamp) of the same as per this SOP 
are submitted to  GFGNL team, IE and GIS NOC Delhi. 
Note: i) GPS enabled Camera/mobile phone that can record Video with live tracking of LAT LONG (GPS 
Coordinates) and Date/ Time Stamping shall be used by the PIA. Video output resolution should not be less 
than 720dpi 
ii) Since storage on cloud required for Videography which is to be done during Project 
phase. Further virtual inspection is also to be mendate from C NOC. Retantion of the 
data largely dependent on above two factors. Cloud storage shall be provided by PIA  
for videography storage till 100% project completion and 100% go-live or till further 
instruction by GFGNL/DBN. 
 
5.17 MEASUREMENT 
I. 
Measurement Book (MB): The measurement books are to be maintained by the PIA. The entry 
shall be made in ink. No entry shall be erased. If a mistake is made, it should be corrected by 
crossing out the incorrect words or figures and inserting the corrections, the corrections thus 
made shall be initialed & dated by the bidder. The measurement books shall invariably be 
consulted at the time of making final payments to the bidder. Here, Pls consider analogy of 
physical entry with digital entry. The PIA shall provide mobile application for the digital 
measurement book and it is responsibility of the PIA to abide with purpose of measurement / 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 201 of 618 
 
 
 
penalty associated with this work. 
II. 
Method of recording of nomenclature of items: Complete nomenclature of items, as given in the 
agreement need not be reproduced in the measurement book for recording the measurement 
but corresponding item code as provided, shall be used. 
III. 
The measurements of various items of work shall be taken and recorded in the measurements 
book. The measurements shall be taken and recorded by bidder which will be countersigned by 
the authority appointed by GFGNL. The PIA shall be directly responsible for supervision of work 
and for accuracy of 100% of measurements. The IE will be responsible for conducting 
Acceptance Test (A/T) check of measurements at different locations on sample basis. The PIA 
shall re-do the work, wherever, the IE finds deviation from the entries in MB by the PIA or GFGNL 
at any subsequent stage during contract period. During subsequent inspection by GFGNL or any 
other agency, in case the sample measured data does not match with the measurement book 
entry up to a lesser depth of 5cm, penalty (equal to amount of difference of payment , so reduced 
due to lesser depth ) shall be levied in addition to the reduction of payment due to lesser depth 
as per the approved formulae on each such default instance on the payment due for the link 
(waiver of penalty, if warranted, shall be decided by GFGNL on case to case basis) . The spirit 
is to ensure correct recording in the measurement book by PIA. GFGNL, on behalf of DIGITAL 
BHARAT NIDHI(DBN), reserve the right to get the work done at the risk and cost of the PIA in 
case of lesser depth cases. 
IV. 
Method of measurement: The measurement of the work shall be done activity-wise as and 
when the item of work is ready for measurement. The methods of measurement of various items 
are enumerated as under: 
• Measurement of Depth of Trenches. The cable route shall be divided into a number of 
segments each of maximum 200 Meters length bounded by identifiable landmarks at both the 
ends of the segments. If landmarks are not available, length of segment may be maintained at 
200 Meters. The depth of trenching and ducting of OFC should be audited with IE or any of the 
third party agency nominated by the GFGNL , and approved based on recommendation by IE or 
any third party audit report after GFGNL due process .The measurement of depth shall be 
recorded at each point of measurement (POM) in the measurement book in Meters in the 
multiples of 5 cms. For example, 97 cms will be recorded as 95 cms and 103 cms as 105 cms. 
This will be by using mround formula in excel/ from backend software.The points of 
measurements shall be at a distance of 10 Meters starting from 0 (Zero) Meter. For example, if 
the length of segment is 75 Meters, the POMs shall be at 0 M, 10 M, 20 M, 30 M, 40 M, 50 M, 
60 M, and 70 M. The last POM shall be at 75th M to be recorded against residual POM. Normally 
the workers tend to dig shallow trenches due to effort involved. As standard depth of the trench 
is important for future life and protection of cables, this tendency has to be discouraged. 
• Measurement of lengths and profiles of strata and protection. The measurements of length 
of trenches are on running Meter basis, irrespective of type of soil encountered while digging. 
The type of protection utilized (item code – wise) to include RCC Half Round and Full Round 
Pipe, DWC HDPE Pipe, GI Pipe, MS Weld Mesh etc in a segment shall be recorded in the 
measurement book in the sheet provided for this purpose. 
• Measurement of length of cable. The length of cables laid in trenches, through pipes and 
through ducts shall be measured by use of OTDR for the purpose of accuracy of the identification 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 202 of 618 
 
 
 
of cuts during O&M. The payment for such laying/trenching as per price schedule shall be 
made as per the RODO Meter readings and not as per the OTDR readings. The length should 
be cross verified with the marking of lengths on the cables. The lengths shall be recorded in 
sheet provided in the measurement book. 
• Measurement of other items. The measurement/ numerical details of other items shall be 
recorded in the sheets provided for respective items viz.  
— Digging of joint pit/manholes and preparation of chambers along with details of its dimensions 
and location. 
— Fixing, Painting and sign writing of route/joint indicators.  
— Termination of Cable in equipment room and no. of joints.  
— Record splice loss details for each joint. 
• The bidder shall sign all the measurement recorded in the measurement book. This will be 
considered as an acceptance by the bidder, of measurements recorded in the MB. In case bidder 
fails to attend at the measurements or fails to countersign or to record the difference within a 
week, then in any such events the measurements taken by IE shall be final and binding on the 
bidder and the bidder shall have no right to dispute the same. In case of any discrepancy in the 
measurement book between the Independent Engineer (IE) and the bidder, the parties shall 
engage in mutual discussions to reconcile the differences. The agreed outcome shall be 
documented and submitted for final confirmation by GFGNL. 
• Measurement of the work of cable for calculation of laying /trenching will be taken equal to the 
length of the pipe/ duct (as measured in the RODO meter) through which the cable has been 
pulled and not the total length of the cable pulled through pipe/duct. 
• Uploading of Depth Photographs: The IE responsible for verification of MB shall take the 
photographs of the depth measurement being done at every 100 m in case of open trench work 
and at the entry / exit points in case of HDD method using BharatNet GIS App and upload the 
same on GIS platform. 
• Compilation of the Measurement Book needs to be on real time basis while the work is being 
carried out. 
• The details noted by the Contractor in the notebooks will be entered in the proper MB format in 
the computer on weekly basis and shared with GFGNL. These shall be checked by IE 
progressively so that as soon as the work of the route is complete, the MB is also ready.

clause, “on demand” shall mean those villages where a minimum demand of five (5) home fiber

State.

c) Following guidelines/ technical specifications shall be followed by the PIA: -  
i. 
The PIA shall use 6F Overhead OFC with structural cabling and all accessories and will 
applicable TEC GR(85200:2022 with latest Amended if any)) as mentioned in the table of 
TEC GRs in Annexure. Last Mile connectivity shall be implemented with 6F Aerial Drop Cable. 
However, the TEC GR mentioned for 12F/ 24F is applicable for 6F cable also allowed. For 
Last mile connectivity for villages 6F is required per GP.  
ii. 
In aerial fibre connectivity if the pole does not have requisite bearing strength, then the LMCA 
will have to bring and set up his own 7 meter RCC poles dedicated for the OFC installation 
along with necessary accessories as per the Engineering Instructions. 
iii. 
The OFC shall be laid using existing Electricity poles  with required accessories wherever 
feasible and approved. TEC GR Standard No.: TEC 87060:2017 2024 including its latest 
Amended, if any, may be referred. 
iv.

meetings, and feasibility studies,etc. 
v. 
Wherever, such electricity poles are not available/used, the PIA is required to erect wooden/ 
G.I. 7 Meter RCC poles at the required intervals so that the OFC withstands normal climatic 
disturbances. 
vi. 
Wherever the existing electricity poles are not available; the PIA shall erect a 7 Meter RCC 
pole. Payment of the quoted/ finalized price, of the Price schedule of related line items, shall 
be made for such RCC Poles, including supply, installation and O&M for the entire contract 
period, on uploading of the video as per specifications. The PIA shall have to replace such 
poles damaged for any reason whatsoever during the contract period without any additional 
cost to GFGNL. 
vii. 
It is the PIA's responsibility to maintain &  manage overhead Cable without dieluting uptime/ 
SLA.  
viii. 
The PIA is required to terminate such OFC at an appropriate location in the village in a

RFP requirements) and at the GP FDMS/FTB from where connectivity extended to revenue 
villages either with a new mini-OLT or using splitters and the mini- OLT installed at the GP.

The PIA shall also be liable to maintain the above arrangement till the completion of the entire

5.19.2 Scope of Work (SoW) for GFGNL 
 
I.GFGNL shall bear and support the payment of power consumption charges at the Gram Panchayat 
(GP) locations. Coordination with the concerned electricity departments for payment release of  
connections shall be within the scope of GFGNL.However, during the O&M period, in the event of 
any power outage, the responsibility for coordination with the respective electricity authorities for 
restoration of power supply shall lie with the PIA.The PIA shall ensure that power is utilized strictly 
for project-related infrastructure and operations. Any unauthorized usage, misuse, diversion of 
electricity, or involvement in fraudulent practices such as meter tampering, illegal connections, or 
usage beyond approved purposes shall be strictly prohibited. 
In case any such malpractice or fraudulent activity is detected: 
a. 
The PIA shall be solely responsible and liable for all penalties, fines, legal 
consequences, and recovery of losses imposed by the electricity department or any 
statutory authority. 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 212 of 618 
 
 
 
b. 
GFGNL shall not bear any financial or legal liability arising out of such acts. 
c. 
GFGNL reserves the right to impose additional penalties, initiate contractual 
action, or terminate the agreement as per applicable terms and conditions of the 
contract. 
The PIA shall also maintain proper records/logs of power usage where required and fully cooperate 
with inspections or audits by GFGNL or statutory authorities. 
II.Any replacement or provisioning of Optical Network Terminals (ONTs) for horizontal customer 
connectivity shall be strictly compatible with the make and model of the parent Optical Line Terminal 
(OLT) deployed in the network. Similarly, all other active devices, including but not limited to Wi-Fi 
CPEs and associated equipment, shall be interoperable and fully compatible with the existing 
network infrastructure and devices to ensure seamless integration and performance. Further, the 
selection, procurement, and deployment of such equipment shall comply with all applicable 
Government procurement policies, guidelines, and standards. 
III.As a general principle, GFGNL shall not permit tapping, branching, or any form of unauthorized 
access to: 
• 
Existing Optical Fiber Cable (OFC) infrastructure laid for Gram Panchayat (GP) 
connectivity; and 
• 
Newly laid OFC infrastructure for GP-to-GP, GP-to-Sub-Block, or Sub-Block-to-Sub-
Block network connectivity. 
The primary objective is to preserve the integrity, redundancy, and reliability of the Sub-Block and 
GP ring architecture and to ensure uninterrupted network performance. 
However, the existing fiber infrastructure laid for horizontal customer connectivity from GP 
locations may be utilized by the new PIA for extending services to customers, subject to: 
• 
Field feasibility and technical validation; and 
• 
Prior written approval from the competent authority of GFGNL. 
Notwithstanding the above, GFGNL reserves the sole and absolute right, at its discretion, to permit 
tapping, modification, or alteration of the network topology or transmission media, based on: 
• 
Valid technical or operational justification; and 
• 
Considerations of long-term sustainability, scalability, and ease of governance of the 
network. 
Any such modification shall be undertaken only with prior written approval of GFGNL and in 
compliance with prescribed standards, and the PIA shall ensure that such changes do not 
adversely impact network performance, redundancy, or service quality. 
Unauthorized tapping or alteration of the network shall be treated as a material breach of contract 
and may result in penalties, suspension, or termination of the agreement, as deemed appropriate 
by GFGNL. 
IV.GFGNL shall not pay any extra cost for transportation of the delivered items for installation, 
commission and O&M of the respective locations.

selected PIA, and will be calculated per GP on a monthly basis as per SLA parameters given below.

hours, the standard working hours shall be from 06:00 AM to 08:00 PM, and non-working hours from

working hours may be considered, subject to submission of valid supporting evidence and approval 
from GFGNL. 
III.For the purpose of these calculations a connection failure shall be defined as a last mile end CPE 
being unable to connect to the GFGNL network. 
IV.GFGNL will pay to selected Bidder on discovered O&M charges of any particular active site / 
location every year as an O&M charge for operation & maintenance activities for that location.

5.19.3 5.19.4 OPEX Payment 
I.O&M payments for last mile enterprise and horizontal customer connectivity shall be made in 
accordance with the Payment Terms of the GFGNL network, subject to compliance with applicable 
Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and deductions of penalties, as specified in this RFP. 
II.The PIA shall be responsible for providing O&M services to all existing customers connected under 
the GFGNL network. Payment for such services shall be made based on the rates discovered under 
Financial Table 1C of the Financial Bid. 
III.The PIA shall submit valid quarterly invoices for O&M services rendered to last mile enterprise and 
horizontal customers. All payments shall be processed after verification and shall be subject to 
applicable SLA compliance and deduction of penalties as per the terms and conditions of this RFP. 
Payment Terms 
a) All invoices shall be subject to verification and certification by GFGNL before release of payment. 
b) Payment shall be released within 45 days from the date of submission of complete and approved 
invoice along with required supporting documents. 
c) Rates quoted by the Bidder shall remain firm and fixed for the entire contract period, and no 
escalation shall be permitted under any circumstances. 
d) All payments shall be released after certification of delivery, installation and acceptance 
tests per the Deliverables. 
e) All payments shall be made in Indian rupees only (INR). 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 216 of 618 
 
 
 
f) Payment shall be released against the invoices raised by PIA on providing all relevant documents 
timely, including preventive, corrective measures, duly signed and approved by GFGNL

g) Payment shall be subject to deductions of any amount for which the supplier is liable under the 
RFP conditions. Further, all payments shall be made subject to deduction of applicable taxes and 
other Government levies like TDS (Tax Deduction at Source) and etc., as per the current Income-

h) All payments shall be released only after deducting all SLA Penalties as applicable. 
 
5.19.4 5.19.5  VIP/ Major / Ad-Hoc Events 
 
a) GFGNL reserves the absolute and unconditional rights, at its sole discretion, to require the 
selected PIA/Bidder to provide support for the development, deployment, operation, and 
maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure for temporary VIP event connectivity. 
The selected PIA/Bidder shall be mandatorily obliged to comply with such requirements, 
including provisioning of resources, manpower, and services, without demur or delay, as 
and when directed by GFGNL, under the same terms and conditions of the Contract. No 
additional claims, objections, or refusals shall be entertained in this regard. 
b) The events in the government functions are highly sensitive and related to VIPs and hence, 
as a creadible bidder it is expected that the link as well as other necessary items limited to 
connectivity is the basic expectation from the bidder. The Bidder may be custodian of the 
spare assets and certainly bidder will be owner of the any new asset of that particular event. 
c) Timeline will be immediate basis (maximum to 24 Hrs to 48 Hrs) for deploy connectivity on 
temporary basis as per the requirement of GFGNL’s customer. 
d) For New connectivity PIA may opt for either aerial method or through proper UG method or 
through Wireless connectivity based on the site feasibility and service requirements, 
keeping the 100% network availability as the design criteria. For connectivity media GFGNL 
shall be consulted prior to the execution by the PIA for the network media. 
e) Selected bidder has to maintain and reserve the sufficient spares materials in advance for these 
type of connectivity requirements. 
f) At the time of event, bidder has to ensure the 24*7 surveillance of the event and has to maintain 
100% service network uptime. For this, sufficient resources field and backend support team for 
online close monitoring has to arrange without any additional cost to GFGNL. Failure to this 
penalty will be deducted 10% of service cost per instance of each site. 
g) For Site integration, payment will be given based on the rates mentioned in following table rate 
card mentioned in below VIP/Adhoc/ Major table. 
h) At the end of event, dismantle of site will be in scope of bidder with immediate basis or as 
instructed by the event authorized agency or as informed from the GFGNL.

5.21 INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE TESTING 
 
I. 
During the Project, GFGNL shall have the right to inspect, test and audit the network 
infrastructure and modalities across processes to construct, operate and maintain the network 
till Gram Panchayat (GP) during construction and operation period i.e. throughout \the 
lifecycle of the project. 
II. 
For determining that the Development Works and/or the Upgradation Works conform to the 
Agreement, the IE shall require the PIA to carry out or cause to be carried out tests, at such 
time and frequency and in such manner as may be specified by the IE from time to time in 
accordance with Good Industry Practice, Specifications and Standards, and Acceptance 
Testing Template for quality assurance. 
III. 
These tests would include testing of all the installed active and passive electronics and 
passive infrastructure along with its additional items deployed under construction and 
upgradation of the network infrastructure as per the scope of work. 
IV. 
This shall also include all network links along with testing of network traffic from the Block to 
Gram Panchayat (GP), SDC/NOC to Block, SDC/NOC to GP, GP to Village, SDC/NOC to 
village and further to NOC implemented / leveraged for this project and BharatNet Delhi and 
Bangalore NOC. 
V. 
The PIA shall perform and facilitate the following with regards to testing activities: 
A. Supply of products/material or network infrastructure: 
I. 
During the Contract Period, the PIA shall obtain from Original Equipment Manufacturers 
(OEM), the relevant certificates or documents with relevant test results, certifying that the 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 219 of 618 
 
 
 
product / material supplied for the Project conforms to the Specifications and Standards and 
design requirements as per provisions set forth in Technical specification section.  
II. 
The records of relevant certificates shall be maintained by the PIA throughout the Contract 
Period.Submit the same to GFGNL and the IE within 7 days of receipt of such certificates or 
documents from OEMs. 
III. 
In case the product / material supplied for the Project does not conform to the Specifications 
and Standards or is deficient in terms of relevant certificates /documents / test results, as 
inspected by GFGNL or IE, then the costs to be incurred on any replacement of such product 
/ material shall be borne solely by the PIA. 
 
B. Deployment of products/ material or network infrastructure 
 
i. The acceptance testing (AT) of the New Network and upgradation of Existing Network shall 
be carried out as per the Acceptance Testing Schedule issued by QA and GFGNL which can 
be accessed online from the website of QA and GFGNL. As validated by the IE, such tests 
along with Acceptance Testing Template shall be designed in conformance with the provisions 
set forth under the section of technical specification of OEM mentioned in this RFP, 
Specifications and Standards and Good Industry Practice.  
ii. The fixed acceptance testing template (AT format) should be submit by PIA in consultation 
with the IE/GFGNL within first week of offered sub-block/GP to avoid any delay. 
iii. Prior to Final Acceptance Testing (FAT), the PIA shall conduct end-to-end traffic testing from 
SNOC/NOC to Gram Panchayat (GP) and village endpoints to validate performance 
parameters including latency, jitter, packet loss, throughput, QoS, and failover, in accordance 
with OEM technical specifications, acceptance testing template, and good industry practice. 
iv. The PIA shall, no later than 30 (thirty) days prior to the likely completion of the construction, 
notify the IE and GFGNL of its intent to subject the infrastructure to tests. 
v. Further, no later than 10 (ten) days prior to the actual date of tests, the PIA shall furnish 
detailed inventory and particulars of all works and equipment forming part of the project to the 
IE and GFGNL. 
vi. In the event of the PIA and the IE failing to mutually agree on the dates for conducting the 
tests, the PIA shall fix the dates by not less than 10 (ten) working days’ notice to the IE, and 
in the event the IE delays the tests hereunder, GFGNL shall ensure that tests are completed 
in time either by the IE or any substitute thereof. 
vii. The PIA shall progressively self-conduct and perform Preliminary Acceptance Testing(PAT) 
for network infrastructure being created as per the scope of work. 
viii. All tests shall be conducted in accordance with Acceptance Testing Template duly approved 
by GFGNL at the cost and expense of the PIA. The IE shall undertake the tests only when all 
the Gram Panchayat (GP) offered for testing are visible in the NOC(GFGNL- NMS). 
ix. Once the PIA performs the PAT, it shall offer network infrastructure within a Block subject to 
minimum 10% Gram Panchayat (GP) completed and pinged from the Central NOC or visible 
in SNOC, for testing purposes to the IE for Final Acceptance Test (FAT). Inspection work for 
FAT within a Block shall be offered only after completion of PAT of the route and site location 
by the PIA. 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 220 of 618 
 
 
 
x. The schedule for such testing shall be based on a project plan and the timelines for the same 
shall be agreed between IE and PIA. However, in case of any changes in the schedule or 
plan, PIA shall notify the IE, 10 (ten) working calendar days prior to the scheduled date. 
xi. In pursuance of the provisions of this Agreement, the IE shall conduct visual and physical 
check of the infrastructure at Blocks and Gram Panchayat (GP) and central locations (i.e. 
NOC) to determine that all works, equipment and services forming part thereof conform to the 
provision of this Agreement and the detailed scope of work as defined in this RFP. 
xii. The IE shall perform tests of offered Gram Panchayat (GP) aggregated at Block level in 
accordance with Good Industry Practice, Specifications and Standards, and Acceptance 
Testing Template. Sample sites and its routes to be checked shall be decided by the IE. 
xiii. The PIA shall facilitate the IE in conducting the tests as per approved Acceptance Testing 
Template and/or as per directions of the IE. All reasonable facilities and assistance like testing 
instruments and other test devices including access to drawings and other details shall be 
furnished, by the PIA to the IE and GFGNL. 
xiv. The cost of all associated works regarding testing as per the scope of work such as digging 
pits at sample sites for connectivity across Gram Panchayat (GP), its restoration,and 
arrangement of testing instruments such as OTDR etc. shall be borne by the PIA. 
xv. The IE may also decide to witness, or participate in, any of the tests to be undertaken by the 
PIA for its own quality assurance in accordance with Good Industry Practice,Specification and 
Standards, and in such an event, the PIA shall cooperate with, and provide the necessary 
assistance to, the IE for discharging its functions hereunder. 
xvi. Result of IE’s inspection and audit shall only be valid for Gram Panchayat (GP) which were 
offered for testing under a Block. If PIA offers a Block for inspection more than once, IE and 
GFGNL reserve the right to include or exclude the test of previously completed Gram 
Panchayat (GP) as well. 
xvii. The overall result(s) of the FAT conducted by IE/ GFGNL shall be indicated as "Satisfactory" 
or "Unsatisfactory" as judged at the time of inspection on merits of each case. The results of 
the test shall be jointly signed by the authorised personnel of the PIA and IE. In case of 
classifying the work as “Unsatisfactory”, the PIA shall highlight the reason for non-compliance 
as per the Specifications and Standards set forth under technical specifications of equipment 
sections and Good Industry Practice along with design requirements under the scope of work. 
The results of the FAT conducted shall include submission of all relevant documents such as 
measurement book, Acceptance Testing Template report etc. 
xviii. Further, “Unsatisfactory” cases shall be communicated to the PIA by the IE/ GFGNL for its 
rectification. 
xix. During a FAT, if more than 10% discrepancies across site route or locations across Gram 
Panchayats (GPs) are observed within a Block which may be attributed due to negligence on 
the part of the PIA, under such circumstances, the FAT may be rejected and retesting carried 
out at the PIA’s cost. Repeated failures shall trigger escalation, Second failure: Expanded 
sampling and witnessed testing by IE. Third failure: Full PAT re-certification, extended soak 
testing, and contractual remedies including LD and PBG invocation.Successful traffic testing 
is a condition precedent for FAT acceptance and milestone payments. Provisional 
Acceptance may be granted only if discrepancies are below 10% and GPs are visible in 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 221 of 618 
 
 
 
SNOC, with a jointly signed Punch List with IE. 
xx. Further, the PIA shall get the work redone in a time bound manner and re-submit FAT report 
compliance, upon which IE/ GFGNL shall have to recheck the offered Gram Panchayat (GP) 
and may also extend the sample size of site route or locations across Gram Panchayats (GPs) 
for discrepancies and record its observations. However, if the discrepancies are less than 
10% within a Block, then GFGNL on recommendation of IE shall provide a provisional 
acceptance and issue a Provisional Acceptance Certificate as per provision set forth in this 
Section. 
xxi. However, the issuance of Provisional Acceptance Certificate shall be subjected to the visibility 
of Gram Panchayat (GP) in the State Network Operations Centre (SNOC). In such an event,

Independent Engineer or GFGNL shall not withhold the Provisional Acceptance Certificate for 
reason of any work remaining incomplete if the delay in completion thereof is attributable to 
GFGNL. 
xxii. The primary goal of Acceptance Testing is to ensure that the work (including all the 
components as discussed in the scope of work) meets requirements, standards,

➢ Infrastructure Compliance 
➢ Performance 
➢ Project Documentation  
xxiii. The Successful bidder shall inform the department in writing, as and when the work is

xxvi. The bidder shall co-ordinate and carry any other required test as desired by purchaser.

xxviii. Any procedure delay for approval of AT acceptance by GFGNL, shall not be considered as

xxix. The bidder is required to rectify the shortcomings reported, if any, during the testing. The

xxx. The payment shall be released to the Bidder from the date of successful testing and

xxxi. The bidder shall be required to extend required cooperation including testing of Material/Links

C. Rectification of defects and deficiencies 
 
I. 
The PIA is obligated to rectify the outstanding item or Punch List in a time bound manner to 
receive a Final Acceptance Certificate on the same as per provision set forth in the above 
section,i.e., Deployment of products/ material or network infrastructure-xviii. 
II. 
In this process, the PIA shall comply with the timelines of the construction milestone and 
shall be responsible for delays on the re-work on its scope. 
III. 
In case any inspected or tested components/site route fail to conform to the Specifications 
and Standards and design requirements as per provisions in the RFP, the PIA shall either 
replace the rejected components or make all alterations necessary to meet specification/ 
requirements, without any additional cost to GFGNL. 
IV. 
If any equipment or any part thereof is found to be defective or fails to fulfil the requirements 
as per provisions set forth in this RFP, GFGNL shall give notice to the PIA setting forth 
details of such defects or failure and the PIA shall at their own cost make the defective 
equipment good or alter the same to make it comply with the requirements forthwith, within 
a period not exceeding one month of the initial report.These replacements shall be made by 
the PIA free of all charges at site and route locations. 
V. 
Further, in the entire process the IE/ GFGNL shall make a report of inspections (the 
“Inspection Report”) performed as a part of FAT. The Inspection Report shall state defects 
or deficiencies, if any, with reasonable details and reference to the specifications and 
Standards and design requirements as per provisions set forth in this RFP. 
VI. 
IE shall send a copy of the Inspection Report to GFGNL and the PIA within(seven) days of 
such inspection and upon receipt thereof, the PIA shall rectify and remedy the defects or 
deficiencies, if any, stated in the Inspection Report. 
VII. 
Notwithstanding the foregoing, such inspection or submission of Inspection Report by the 
IE shall not relieve or absolve the PIA of its obligations and liabilities hereunder in any 
manner whatsoever. 
VIII. 
Based on the Inspection report or the defect and deficiencies observed in the Project,the IE/ 
GFGNL shall verify whether remedial measures have brought the Development Works 
and/or the Upgradation Works into compliance with Specifications and Standards and 
design requirements as per provisions set forth in this RFP. 
IX. 
The procedure for closure of defect and deficiencies as reported shall be repeated until such 
development Works and/or the Upgradation Works conform to the Specifications and 
Standards and design requirements as per provisions set forth in this RFP. 
X. 
Further, it is agreed that the tests pursuant to this shall also be undertaken in addition to 
and independent of the tests carried out by the PIA for its own quality assurance in 
accordance with Applicable Laws, Applicable Permits and Good Industry Practice.  
XI. 
It is also agreed that a copy of the results of such tests shall be sent by the PIA to the IE 
forthwith. The costs to be incurred on any test which is undertaken for determining the 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 223 of 618 
 
 
 
rectification of any defect or deficiency in the Development Works and/or the Upgradation 
Works shall be borne solely by the PIA. 
XII. 
Upon successful completion of tests, the IE/ GFGNL shall issue the Completion 
Certificate,as the case may be, in accordance with the provisions in this i.e., Deployment of 
products/ material or network infrastructure-xviii. 
XIII. 
If the IE/ GFGNL certifies to GFGNL and the PIA that it is unable to issue the Completion 
Certificate or Provisional Acceptance Certificate, as the case may be, because of events or 
circumstances on account of which the tests could not be held or had to be suspended,the 
PIA shall be entitled to re-schedule the tests and hold the same as soon as reasonably 
practicable.

required.

other related agencies from the Appointed Date.

applicable by completely following RoW application process of respective agencies. State/SIA 
shall support the PIA in obtaining the same.GFGNL will pay for the ROW charges. In event of 
speeding of the work where ROW charges are minor, if PIA pays for the ROW charges, then 
GFGNL shall reimburse without delay (Monthly basis) after adjusting penalty raised/settled by 
the agency. The any associated penalty is to be settled or to be borne by the PIA. The after 
completion of the work / ROW obligation, it is the duty of PIA to timely collect the ROW charges 
/ Security deposits with utmost seriousness. In case, the collection cycle exceeds beyond 6 (six) 
months without any reason in writing by the PIA, then GFGNL shall deduct the delayed amount 
from running payments without any sympathy.

Contract Period to the State Government (s) or its agencies. Further, any other costs associated

valid proof of payment by the PIA. This includes applicable charges for Right of Way from

5.23 OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE 
 
The breakdown of the contract for maintaining a network after its set up.  
 
I. 
As mentioned in the Factsheet, above, the overall/complete contract duration, including 
Supply, Installation, Testing, Commissioning, and Maintenance, will last for 10 years. 
II. 
Until the entire network is running, any parts that are active will also be maintained, and 
payment for this will be determined on a proportional basis. 
III. 
PIA shall undertake the responsibility for Operations & Maintenance (O&M) of the Existing 
Network including the existing leased OFC of Phase-1 (all the fibres in the cable, although 
only one fibre is used in many cases) & in phase-2 till the same is replaced with the new laid 
network,Incremental OFC laid under BharatNet, Maintenance of existing GPON equipment 
(OLTs, ONTs, all active and passive elements including Solar system) and New deployed 
Network under this RFP will be in the scope of selected bidder.  
IV. 
All expenditure required to perform O&M of the Existing Network and New Network shall be 
the responsibility of the PIA. 
V. 
The PIA shall be required to commence O&M for newly connected individual Gram 
Panchayats (GPs) immediately after the date of commissioning and from the date of handover 
in case of existing BharatNet network. 
VI. 
Beyond 10th year( For contract extension), the equipment which is not EoSL (End of 
Support/Sales Life), can be continued along with the network for O&M as per decision of 
DIGITAL BHARAT NIDHI(DBN)/ DoT/ GFGNL and also with the consensus of PIA. The OPEX 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 228 of 618 
 
 
 
payable after 10th year will be enhanced annually by 4% (i.e. 11th year will have OPEX of 
6.76%, 12th year will be 7.02% and so on) till the continuity of the O&M of the network by PIA. 
VII. 
Government of INDIA has launched CBuD (Call Before You Dig) for synegrgies between 
various stakeholders. PIA shall ensure to use CBuD application by his appointed 
agencies/vendors/employees prior to any field work commencement. Selected PIA shall 
mandatorily ensure to use CBuD applications, rules and compliances by his appointed 
agencies/vendors/employees/subcontractors prior to any field work commencement. 
Penalties will be applied in case of non-compliance as per CBuD. 
VIII. 
A block network will only be considered active (100% go-live) when all 90% of GPs will be 
operational on MPLS network at last mile.Where, Block to be consider as ~2 or 3 Sub-Block 
based on geographical boundaries and connected through dual homed OFC network which 
are to be parented on Master-block,subsequencially the all the GPs of Block as per network 
design principles mentioned above connected in various dual home OFC ring architecture. 
Accordingly, 90% of all GPs of Block are live in IP-MPLS OFC dual home ring architecture 
visible in SNOC/CNOC will be treated as 100% go-live. Further, the aggregate count of GP 
at Sub-Block will be considered at once for the cases of dual home network architecture,i.e., 
the other side of block GP ring will not be considered. 
IX. 
Selected PIA shall undertake the responsibility for Operations & Maintenance (O&M) of the 
all active and passive elements fall under following categories, 
a) Phase-I entire existing infrastructure till the same is replaced with new laid network. 
b) Phase-II Existing Network infrastructure including the shelter infrastructure(Which 
includes stabilizers, racks, and GPON network elements with all releated active and 
passive accessories, splitters, FDMS etc.)immediately after the milestone mentioned 
in the RFP document of Handover-Takeover (HoTo) procedure. 
c) Phase-I infrastructure immediately after completion of own infrastructure of leased 
sections as per milestone. 
d) Intermediate/incremental sections (Connectivity between Phase-I and Phase-II, 
between intermediate island connectivity, ring shortening, etc.) and any other 
additional scope mentioned in this RFP with design approval of IE/GFGNL. 
e) Connecting/Shifting the remaining unconnected Gram Panchayats (GPs) under 
BharatNet Operation and Maintenance (O&M) of the existing as well as the newly 
deployed network, including proactive and reactive maintenance activities. 
f) The establishment of governance framework, and escalation procedures & matrix for 
network and customer support service on 365 x 24 x 7 basis. 
g) PIA shall support on extending access of the Network Management System or other 
equivalent systems along with network performance reports on a mutually agreed basis 
to GFGNL, CNOC-BharatNet Delhi,and Bangalore NOC. 
h) The services provided shall adhere and conform to applicable security policies and 
guidelines issued by DoT/TRAI/GoI/GoG/MeitY/GFGNL - DST. 
i) The PIA shall be responsible and bear costs for replenishment and upgrade of all active 
and passive infrastructure including all ancillaries required for smooth executions and 
operations & maintenance of project across the Contract Period. 
j) In case of any defect, deficiency or deterioration in the Project poses a hazard to safety 


[SIGN OF BIDDER]                                                                                                                Page 229 of 618 
 
 
 
or risk of damage to property, the PIA shall promptly take all reasonable measures for 
eliminating or minimising such danger. 
k) The PIA shall insure all the equipment at GP for theft, damages due to fire, 
flood,earthquake, storm etc for the entire project duration. 
l) The basic Operation and Maintenance Guidelines/ directions released centrally 
through BSNL (RFP Number: MM/BNO&M/BN-III/T-791/2024 or MM/BNO&M/BN-III/T-
857/2025 or latest) to be follow including their corrigendum’s/addenda / clarification

process. Existing Agency will provide necessary handholding and transition support to new

the selected bidder to coordinate end to end with the existing agencies and all relevant 
stakeholders involved in existing project. 
c)

geographical condition or network requirement it may be initiate by Block Wise, lot wise, Route 
wise/GP Wise,district wise and GFGNL will further release the Guideline/SOP once the 
selected PIA will get onboarded. 
d) 
Successful Bidder must align FRT resources with attendance within 12 weeks and in any case, 
if not able to arrange resources, penalty will be applicable as per RFP. 
e) 
Handover/take-over will be conducted on toll-gate basis only.   
 
Toll Gate based approach shall be implemented over period of 180 days for BharatNet 
Phase-I and 90 days for BharatNet Phase-II (considering the overall dependency and 
strengthen the project) in 3 different phases: 
 
Phase 1: The existing PIA will run the operation and Maintenance and the new PIA will get 
the knowledge transfer.   
 
Phase 2: The new PIA will run the operation and Maintenance under the supervision of 
the existing PIA. 
 
Phase 3: Both the party will do the handholding work, documentation and sign-off the 
satisfactory transfer of work. 
 
• 
New Agency/PIA shall be responsible to deploy sufficient manpower for network handover 
activity and do the signoff as per Project & RFP Guideline and both parties (OLD and New 
Agency) sign off report to be submitted at GFGNL Office.

losses where legally permissible.

with end customer. Also, ensure the minimum/no outage on dark fibre customer while working on 
joint chamber for revised splicing during O&M and ensure to inform to dark fibre customer in 
advance for smooth operations and satisfactions of dark fibre customers. As on the date of 
issuance of this RFP, GFGNL has leased approximately 30,000 km of dark fibre to various 
customers, including Telecom Service Providers (TSPs), Internet Service Providers (ISPs), and 
other entities. Additional leasing arrangements are currently under progress. Considering that the

least 50% GPs are having optical power as specified above.

condition” (optical power is in the range -8 dBm to -25 dBm) progressively. However, at the end

the network. i.e., after completion of milestone in section above)  from appointed date, the entire 
network shall be deemed to be handover to the selected PIA on as is where is basis. 
p)   O&M Payment for Non-functional routes after handover payment shall be made only for the routes 
which are made operational by PIA. 
q)   In those blocks, where complete OFC network of the block is taken over by PIA and all the GPs 
are not up, on date of such taking over, the PIA has to make additional 5% GPs of the block as 
operational every month after 2 months from such taking over date, till all the GPs are made 
operational. A penalty of Rs. 5,000/- per month per GP shall be levied and deducted from the 
O&M invoice, for such shortfall of achieving 5% addition in operational GP count of the block, 
every month from 4th month of taking over date. The GPs becoming operational as per NoC 
report, will be counted for AMC payments from date of becoming operational. 
r)  In critical cases involving the shifting of a GP, to avoid any delay in service restoration, the PIA 
shall be solely responsible for arranging temporary aerial connectivity within 2 (two) days(if 
existing is in linear temporary connectivity in linear or if already is in ring temporary shifting shall 
also be in ring) from the date of intimation by GFGNL or authorized Government official of GP. 
The temporary connectivity shall remain operational until the permanent connectivity is restored. 
Further, upon receipt of intimation from GFGNL regarding confirmation of the final location, the 
PIA shall complete the shifting of the end site from the temporary location to the permanent site 
within 10 (ten) calendar days. It is the responsibility of PIA to plan shifting at permanent location 
properly without disruption of any downtime of services.  If the PIA fails to complete the Shifting 
Event within the prescribed timeline for reasons not constituting Force Majeure and not caused 
by GFGNL, LD of INR 2,500 (Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundreds) per day of delay, capped 
at INR 25,000 (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) per Shifting Event, shall apply.

b. Issue Resolution: The new O&M Bidder shall resolve any issues that arise during the post-
handover period, with the support of the existing O&M Bidder. 
c. Final Handover: The existing O&M Bidder shall formally hand over the network operations, 
maintenance, and troubleshooting responsibilities to the new O&M Bidder.

VII. 
Conversion of Aerial OFC Network to Underground (UG) including route rectification 
a) The selected Bidder shall be responsible for conversion of existing aerial Optical Fiber 
Cable (OFC) network to Underground (UG) infrastructure, as detailed below: 
i. Approximately ~40% of Phase-I network and ~8% of Phase-II network, 
aggregating to ~11,000 km of OFC network, presently in aerial condition or 
damaged. 351 Rs.(Including Taxes) Per day per GP willbe given to PIA  for 
O&M of existing OFC network including electronics, route rectification, Aerial to 
Underground conversion, and to achieve fiberization principles stated in RFP 
up to initial 3 years from the appointed date and/or till the 100% Go-live 
whichever is earlier, shall be considered for aerial to UG conversion with the 
same size of existing UG OFC specification and given EI. 
ii. The conversion of the aforesaid network into UG infrastructure shall be 
mandatorily completed within the first three (3) years of the project duration. 
b) The cost for aerial-to-UG conversion during the initial three (3) years shall be deemed 
to be included within the O&M rates, as follows: 
i. INR 351 (Including Taxes) per GP for Phase-I and Phase-II 
ii. No additional payment shall be admissible for this scope during the initial three-
year period. 
c) The Bidder shall ensure near 100% (not less then 95%) conversion to UG within the 
completion of three (3) years from the agreement signed date.Upon completion, the 
Bidder shall submit a formal undertaking, duly certified by the Independent Engineer 
(IE), confirming compliance with the UG conversion requirement. 
d) The Bidder shall submit weekly progress reports in a format prescribed by GFGNL. 
Further, for this, Periodic inspections and audits shall be conducted by: Independent 
Engineer (IE), and/or GFGNL, and/or any other Third-party agency nominated by 
GFGNL.The Bidder shall extend full cooperation during such audits and inspections. 
e) After completion of the initial three (3) years and/or after 100% Go-Live, any remaining 
aerial network (not more than 5% of initial) or additional UG conversion requirements 
shall be addressed through a “Change Management Process”. Based on observations 
and recommendations of GFGNL / IE / authorized third-party auditors, specific change 
requests may be approved.Approved works under change management shall be 
executed based on discovered rates through this tender. 
f) Newly Approved conversion works under change management shall be completed by 
the Bidder within forty-five (45) days from the date of approval. Payment shall be 
released only upon satisfactory completion and certification. 
g) In case of failure to complete approved works within the stipulated timeline, a penalty 
of 5% of the value per week of the pending work/section shall be levied.

5.23.4 NETWORK INVENTORY 
a. 
The PIA would be required to maintain an inventory of all the components used in the network 
and the spares available at the different levels and locations in the ERP software. Warehouse 
for keeping the spares at BHQ/DHQ shall be in scope bidder. 
a. The PIA would be required to maintain an inventory of all the components used in the network 
and the spares available at the different levels and locations in the proposed inventory and 
asset management tool. Warehouse for keeping the spares at BHQ/DHQ shall be in scope 
bidder. 
b. PIA shall prepare and maintain asset and/or inventory records listing the assets as per site 
locations required for performing the O&M and the same shall be shared with GFGNL every 
quarter and as & when asked.  
c. At individual site, installed/integrated network elements inventory list should be stick properly 
and visible at shelter,SDC,GP or the sites those are part of the BharatNet Phase-III network 
under this RFP scope. 
d. PIA has to develop centralized automated change management tool, which will shows the 
overall online inventory tool, which includes minimum but not limited to materials serial 
number, mac address, inventory used location, Quantity, summary report, etc. as and when 
required and will get reviewed every quarter first week. SOP will be shared alongwith workflow 
requirement for approval from GFGNL stakeholders to selected PIA once onboarded to 
GFGNL. 
e. The PIA shall raise a request to reorder / replacements / replenishments / spares in case the
